story.head: Open season on the Kraken’s net
paras: The Hurricanes won the teams’ first meeting this season, 4-1 in Seattle on Thursday. The Canes have won three straight, while the Kraken are 9-7-1. Going in, the Kraken are fourth in the Pacific (22nd in the NHL) and the Hurricanes first in the Metropolitan (tied for first).
The Kraken’s record (.559) is running ahead of what their chances are worth (.436), largely thanks to their finishing. The Hurricanes’ record (.800) is about what their chances are worth.

The Kraken roll their lines more evenly than anyone (1st) and keep dangerous shots away (1st), but rarely threaten on the penalty kill (32nd). The Hurricanes, by contrast, create chances on the penalty kill (1st). Seattle has allowed 3.59 goals a game, the fourth most in the league. The Hurricanes take away shots from the point (lowest) and give up a lot of dangerous shots (32nd). Carolina has scored 4.10 goals a game, the most in the league, and allowed 2.25, the second fewest. The Hurricanes are likely to get plenty of pucks to the net against the Kraken, and the Kraken’s knack for getting shots through meets a team that blocks a lot.

Berkly Catton (5 G / 9 A / 14 P in 17 GP) leads the Kraken in scoring, and Frédérick Gaudreau (8 G / 3 A / 11 P in 17 GP) has a team-high eight goals. Sebastian Aho (12 G / 16 A / 28 P in 20 GP) leads the Hurricanes in scoring and is tied for seventh in the NHL, with nine points in his last five games. Logan Stankoven (11 G / 9 A / 20 P in 20 GP) is next in line, with eight points in his last five games.

Pyotr Kochetkov (11-1-0 / .920 SV% in 12 GS) has been terrific for Carolina and is expected to start. Seattle has two options in net: Philipp Grubauer (5-4-1 / .887 SV% in 9 GS) and Joey Daccord (4-3-0 / .881 SV% in 8 GS). Grubauer has started six of their last ten games, including the last one on Thursday. It’s anyone’s guess who gets the net.

At home, Rod Brind'Amour likes to send Robinson, Kotkaniemi and Martinook out against opponents’ fourth lines, so watch for them against Nyman, Meyers and Winterton. Elsewhere, the Hurricanes usually control more of the chances than the Kraken do.
